ui.m.home.t: LYNX SHARE: a lightweight open-source DAW that opens FL Studio and Ableton Live projects
ui.m.home.d: LYNX SHARE is a free, open-source DAW for Windows, macOS and Linux with FL Studio's way of working: Channel rack, Piano roll, Playlist and Mixer. It opens .flp, .als and .flm projects and exports .flp and .als.

ui.fe.pluL: When you open an .flp, each FL Studio native plugin is replaced by an engine written for LYNX SHARE and compared against the original running unmodified. The dot says how close it is: Exact means bit-identical output. {0} of the {1} FL Studio entries below are Exact or Near-exact.
ui.hero.pill: Free & open source · Windows · macOS · Linux
ui.home.lead: LYNX SHARE is a DAW that works the way FL Studio does: Channel rack, Piano roll, Playlist and Mixer, with the same shortcuts. It opens FL Studio projects (.flp), Ableton Live sets (.als) and FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm), and exports .flp and .als back. It is free under the AGPL-3.0 and still an alpha.
ui.home.what1: You build patterns in the Channel rack and the Piano roll, arrange them with audio and automation clips in the Playlist, and mix in the Mixer: up to 127 insert tracks with 10 effect slots each, sends and sidechain. If you know FL Studio, the windows, mouse gestures and shortcuts are where you expect them.
ui.home.what2: Projects from other programs open directly. An .flp comes in with its channels, samples, patterns, arrangement, automation and mixer, and FL Studio's native plugins are replaced by LYNX SHARE's own engines. Live 11 and 12 sets open too, and their Session clips land in an optional clip grid with scenes (View › Layout style).
ui.home.what3: Third-party plugins load as VST3 and CLAP on every system, plus Audio Units on macOS and LV2 on Linux. VST2 plugins load on Windows and Linux, and on Windows 32-bit plugins run through a bridge.
ui.home.miss: It is an alpha, so expect bugs and keep backups. Not every FL Studio plugin is recreated exactly: the plugin list gives the status of each one. Live's own devices are not converted, and .flm import leaves out FL Studio Mobile's effects. The Windows build is not code-signed and the macOS build is not notarized yet, so both systems warn the first time you open it.

ui.home.capPl: Playlist. Pattern, audio and automation clips on tracks, with markers and several arrangements per project.
ui.home.capPr: Piano roll. Notes, slides, chords and scales, with velocity and pitch lanes.
ui.home.capMx: Mixer. Inserts, sends, sidechain and delay compensation.
ui.home.shotsN: Screenshots are from LYNX SHARE's own demo project in the current release. More on the Features page.
ui.home.src1: LYNX SHARE is written in C++20 with JUCE 8. The code, the tests and the notes on every FL Studio behaviour it reproduces are in one public repository. FL Studio and Live were studied from the outside and the code was written from scratch: nothing from Image-Line or Ableton is in it.
ui.home.src2: Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. Several fixes in recent releases came from users.
ui.home.srcN: Build instructions for each system are in docs/SETUP_DEV.md.
ui.sig.title: Code signing policy
ui.sig.p1: Free code signing provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.
ui.sig.p2: Release files are built from the public source by GitHub Actions, and every signing request is approved by hand.
ui.sig.roles: Authors, reviewers and approvers: Ka1-S (repository owner).
ui.sig.pp: This program will not transfer any information to other networked systems unless specifically requested by the user or the person installing or operating it. Privacy policy
ui.sig.cr2: Opt-in only. After a crash or freeze LYNX SHARE asks before sending a report (Settings › General › Crash reports: Ask / Always send / Never send). A report holds a random id, the LYNX SHARE version, the operating system, CPU, graphics cards and drivers, screen size, audio device and settings, the crash or freeze file, the session's last 60 steps, and the names and versions of the third-party plugins that were loaded. User names in paths become <user>, and file names are left out unless you tick "include file names". No audio, projects or samples, no machine name and no IP address are stored. Reports are used only to fix bugs. To have one deleted, open an issue with its id (LYNX SHARE shows it after sending; every sent id is also listed in crash-reports/sent.log in LYNX SHARE's settings folder).

ui.fe.sub: What is in the current release, window by window, and where it still falls short. The wiki explains how to use each part.
ui.fe.winL: The layout follows FL Studio: Browser, Channel rack, Piano roll, Playlist and Mixer, each opened and closed with the same keys as there.
ui.fe.plP: Pattern, audio and automation clips on tracks. Right-click a clip for split, chop, merge, reverse, normalize and fit to tempo.
ui.fe.plA: Several arrangements in one project, markers and time selection
ui.fe.plB: Automation clips with curves for any knob or fader, and optional automation lanes under tracks
ui.fe.plC: Audio recording with loop takes and comping
ui.fe.plD: Video tracks with a timecode ruler (export with video needs FFmpeg)
ui.fe.crP: A step sequencer with one row per instrument. Each channel has volume, pan, mute and solo, and each pattern its own name, colour and length.
ui.fe.crA: Swing, cut groups, an arpeggiator and layer channels
ui.fe.crB: The PC keyboard plays notes like a piano
ui.fe.prP: Configurable snap, chords and scales, 16 note colours, note groups, and slide and porta notes.
ui.fe.prA: Lanes for velocity, pan and pitch under the notes
ui.fe.prC: Quantize, strum, arpeggiate and randomize tools
ui.fe.mxP: Up to 127 insert tracks. Each has 10 effect slots with dry/wet, sends with levels, a built-in EQ and delay compensation.
ui.fe.mxA: Sidechain from one menu on any effect with a side input
ui.fe.mxB: VCA faders and groups that fold
ui.fe.mxC: Moving a track keeps its sends, sidechains and automation
ui.fe.auP: Any knob or fader of a channel, the mixer, an effect or a plugin can become a clip with points and curves. MIDI controllers can be linked to any parameter, and modulators (an LFO or a random source) move a knob around its own value.
ui.fe.clP: An optional layout (View › Layout style) puts a grid of clips and scenes next to the Playlist, in the manner of Ableton Live's Session view. Clips have launch modes, quantisation, legato, loop and follow actions.
ui.fe.clP2: Live sets bring their Session clips into this grid, and exporting an .als writes the grid back. The pattern layout stays the default and nothing changes in it.
ui.fe.fmL: An imported project is saved as a .lynx file, and the original is never changed. After each import a report lists what was approximated or left out.
ui.fe.fmFlp: Channels, samples, patterns, arrangement, automation and mixer come in. FL Studio's native plugins play on LYNX SHARE's engines (see the list below). On export, what FL Studio does not have is rendered to audio or left out.
ui.fe.fmAls: Tracks, clips, mixer settings, automation and VST2 / VST3 plugins. Simpler, Sampler and drum racks become samplers. Live's own effects are dropped and racks keep their first chain. On export, LYNX SHARE's own instruments and effects are not converted.
ui.fe.fmFlm: Arrangement, samples, drum kits and DirectWave programs. FL Studio Mobile's effects are not imported yet.
ui.fe.fmMid: As a new project, or into the current one from the Piano roll.
ui.fe.fmAud: WAV at 16-bit, 24-bit or 32-bit float. Stems: one file per mixer insert, per channel or per Playlist track.
ui.fe.synC: The built-in synth: 3 oscillators, a multimode filter with keytracking, FM and ring modulation, envelopes and 4 LFOs.
ui.fe.eqC: Facet EQ: 8 bands, cuts up to 96 dB/oct, dynamic bands and a pre/post analyser, at zero latency.
ui.fe.ins1: Sampler with zones, slices, time-stretch and disk streaming
ui.fe.ins2: LYNX Soundfont, an SF2 / SF3 player
ui.fe.ins3: Built-in drums: kick, snare, hat, clap
ui.fe.ins4: Note effects (sequencer, key mapper, keyboard splitter) and controllers (X-Y, envelope, voltage)
ui.fe.fx1: EQs, compressor with sidechain, limiter, gate
ui.fe.fx3: Vocoder, pitch correction, pitch and frequency shifters
ui.fe.fx4: Patcher: a node graph of effects, instruments and plugins
ui.fe.fx5: Hardware insert for outboard gear, with delay compensation
ui.fe.host1: VST3 and CLAP on every system
ui.fe.host2: Audio Units on macOS, LV2 on Linux, VST2 on Windows and Linux
ui.fe.host3: 32-bit VST2 and VST3 on Windows, through a bridge
ui.fe.host4: A plugin can run in its own process, so a crash in it does not take the project down

ui.pl.tm: FL Studio and its plugin names are trademarks of Image-Line Software, used here only to describe compatibility. LYNX SHARE is not affiliated with Image-Line. No Image-Line code or audio data ships with LYNX SHARE; built-in waves are read from your own FL Studio installation.
ui.fe.insL: LYNX SHARE has its own effects that play the role of widely used third-party plugins. If a project uses one of those plugins and it is not installed, the LYNX SHARE effect loads in its slot and the original's settings are kept for when it is back.
ui.cl.tm: Product and company names are trademarks of their respective owners. They are used only to describe compatibility and the role each LYNX SHARE engine plays. LYNX SHARE is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by any of them and contains none of their code, presets, graphics or audio.
ui.fe.demoL: The demo project comes with the program. Every sound in it is from LYNX SHARE's own synths, drums and effects, and the audio below was exported by LYNX SHARE.
ui.media.songp: 124 BPM · kick, clap, reese bass, pad, pluck and supersaw. Click the waveform to seek.
ui.fe.demoN: The video is a slideshow of screenshots over the demo song. It was made for an earlier version, so some windows look different now.
ui.fe.tryT: A step sequencer in the browser
ui.fe.tryL: This is a toy made for this page, not the program: six rows and sixteen steps, to show how the Channel rack's step grid works. Click steps, then press play.
ui.fe.engP: The audio engine spreads channels and mixer tracks across CPU cores, skips channels that are silent and streams long audio files from disk. Measured against FL Studio 2026 on the developer's PC, it used 2.5 to 7 times less RAM and rendered the demo songs 2 to 3 times faster. The method and the numbers are in the benchmark notes; your results will differ.
ui.dlp.sub: Free, with no account, for Windows, macOS and Linux.
ui.dl.hwin: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. The installer needs no admin rights. The executable is not code-signed yet: if SmartScreen warns, choose More info → Run anyway.
ui.dl.portWinP: Unzip to any folder and open LYNX.exe.
ui.dl.store: Windows 10 / 11: also on the Microsoft Store, with automatic updates.
ui.dl.hmac: macOS 11 or newer, Apple Silicon or Intel. The app is not notarized by Apple yet: drag LYNX SHARE to Applications, then the first time right-click it → Open → Open (on macOS 15 or newer: try to open it once, then System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway). Or in Terminal: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/LYNX.app
ui.dl.hlinux: Linux x86_64 with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36 or newer). AppImage: chmod +x LYNX-*.AppImage, then run it (some distros need libfuse2). The .tar.gz has an install.sh that installs for your user with a menu entry.
ui.dlp.all: All releases and checksums on GitHub
ui.dlp.know1: LYNX SHARE is an alpha. It opens, plays and exports whole projects, but it has bugs. Save often, and keep a copy of anything you import from another program.
ui.dlp.know2: Installed versions offer new releases through an Update bar under the toolbar. The Microsoft Store version updates through the Store, and the AppImage through AppImageUpdate or Gear Lever.
ui.dlp.know3: Plugin formats differ per system: VST3 and CLAP everywhere, Audio Units on macOS, LV2 on Linux, VST2 on Windows and Linux. ASIO and the 32-bit plugin bridge are Windows-only.

ui.dlp.reqMac: 11 or newer, Apple Silicon or Intel
ui.dlp.priv: No telemetry and no account. Crash reports are sent only if you agree. Details
ui.faq.a1: Yes. It is free software under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0). You may use, study, modify and redistribute it. Anyone who distributes a modified version must publish its source code under the same licence.
ui.faq.q2: Which systems does it run on?
ui.faq.a2: Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit), macOS 11 or newer (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Linux x86_64 with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36 or newer). The files are on the download page.
ui.faq.q3: Is this FL Studio, or made by Image-Line?
ui.faq.a3: No. LYNX SHARE is an independent program with an FL Studio-style workflow. FL Studio's behaviour and file format were studied clean-room, no Image-Line code was copied, and LYNX SHARE is not affiliated with Image-Line.
ui.faq.q4: Does it open my FL Studio projects, and what is lost?
ui.faq.a4: File › Open... reads .flp files: channels, samples, patterns, arrangements, automation, the Mixer and third-party plugins you have installed. FL Studio's native plugins play on recreated engines, most of them exact or near-exact and a few approximate. FLEX packs are never opened. An import report lists what was approximated or left out. See Coming from FL Studio.
ui.faq.q5: Does it open Ableton Live sets?
ui.faq.a5: Yes, sets saved by Live 11 and 12 (.als): tracks, clips, mixer settings, automation and VST2 or VST3 plugins. Live's own effects are dropped, racks keep their first chain, and Simpler, Sampler and drum racks become LYNX SHARE samplers. See Coming from Ableton Live.
ui.faq.q6: Does it open FL Studio Mobile projects?
ui.faq.a6: Partly. A .flm opens with its arrangement, samples, drum kits and DirectWave programs. FLM's effects are not imported yet.
ui.faq.q7: Can I send a project back to FL Studio or Live?
ui.faq.a7: Yes. File › Export › FL Studio project... writes a .flp, and File › Export › Ableton Live set (.als)... writes a set for Live 12 or Live 11. What the other program does not have is rendered to audio or left out, and a report says which. The limits are on the File formats page.
ui.faq.a8: VST3 and CLAP plugins load on every system. VST2 loads on Windows and Linux, Audio Units on macOS and LV2 on Linux. On Windows, 32-bit VST2 and VST3 plugins run through a bridge. See Plugins.
ui.faq.a9: It is an alpha. It opens, plays and exports whole projects, but it is not yet a replacement for the DAW you rely on every day. Save often and report what breaks.
ui.faq.q10: Why does Windows or macOS warn when I open it?
ui.faq.a10: The Windows executable is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn: click More info, then Run anyway. The macOS app is not notarized by Apple: right-click it and choose Open the first time. The steps are on the Troubleshooting page.
ui.faq.a11: There is no telemetry, analytics, account or licence check. It checks GitHub for a new version (you can turn this off in Settings › General › Updates), and it sends a crash report only if you agree each time or set it to always send. It also connects when you ask for a stem model download or take part in a live online session. The privacy policy has the details.
ui.faq.a12: When a newer version exists, a bar under the toolbar offers Update. The Windows installer version installs it over itself. The portable and macOS versions save the new file to your Downloads folder. The Linux AppImage updates through AppImageUpdate or Gear Lever. The Microsoft Store version is updated by the Store and has no Update button. Release notes are on the updates page.
ui.faq.q13: Which languages does the interface have?
ui.faq.a13: Fifteen: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Dutch, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Spanish and Turkish.
ui.faq.q14: How do I report a bug or contribute?
ui.faq.a14: Open an issue at github.com/Ka1-S/LYNX-SHARE/issues, or use Help › Report a problem... inside the program. The source code is in the same repository, and pull requests from contributors have been merged in past releases.

featured.3x Osc engine: Three-oscillator subtractive synth, FL's classic starting point.
featured.FL Keys engine: Light sampled piano, electric piano and keys; samples from your own FL install.
featured.Gross Beat: Time and volume slicing for stutters, gates and tape stops.
featured.Fruity Limiter: Limiter, compressor and noise gate in one: the master-bus staple.
featured.Parametric EQ: Seven-band parametric EQ, linear-phase mode included.
featured.Soundgoodizer: One knob, four characters: instant loudness and punch.
featured.Fruity Delay 3: Analog-style delay with modulation, diffusion and feedback filtering.
featured.Reeverb 2: Algorithmic reverb, from small rooms to huge halls.
featured.Fruity Compressor: The classic FL compressor, sidechain included.
featured.Epoch Verb: 22 vintage-digital reverb algorithms and three eras of colour; VintageVerb settings carry over.
featured.Nebula: Huge delay-reverb networks: delay, feedback, density, warp and 22 shapes.
featured.Atrium: Rooms and chambers with separate early and late sections and three-band decay.
featured.Foil Plate: Bright plate reverb with instant onset and twelve plate types.
featured.Echoform: Multi-mode echo: tape, bucket brigade, analog, digital, shifter, pitch, reverse; ValhallaDelay settings carry over.

insp.SPL/Transient Designer: Level-independent transient designer: Attack ±15 dB and Sustain ±24 dB from two envelopes, no threshold, plus output, parallel mix, soft-clip guard and a detector high-pass.
insp.Slate Digital (Complete Access)/VCC Chan: Console channel: six measured console models with drive, noise, groups and group bypass, amber VU.
insp.Solid State Logic (Complete Access)/Drum: Drum channel strip: gate, transient shaper, low and high frequency enhancers, listen-mic compressor and 120 process orders.
insp.Solid State Logic (Complete Access)/Guit: Guitar and bass channel strip: phase correction, EQ with filters, five-mode compressor, guitar and bass amps, output mix.
